findings.body:
**Authorization removed on a destructive endpoint.** Dropping `@require_role("admin")` leaves `DELETE /users/<user>` with no access control: any caller who can reach the app can delete any user and get `204`.

Cleanup jobs running as `viewer` need a deliberate authz path (service account, scoped token, or an explicit admin-or-job role check) — not an open delete handler.

```suggestion
@require_role("admin")
```

If viewers must delete, replace the decorator with a check on the *caller* identity (admin or a dedicated cleanup principal), not the path `<user>` target.

summary:
## Verdict

I'd recommend not merging until the authorization removal on `DELETE /users/<user>` is resolved — this is an unauthenticated destructive endpoint with no remaining access control.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `app.py:19` | Removes `@require_role("admin")` from user deletion, leaving the endpoint open to anyone |

## Notes

The PR description frames this as unblocking cleanup jobs that run as the viewer account. Removing the role gate entirely makes `DELETE /users/<user>` callable with no admin check and no replacement authn/authz (service account, API key, internal-only binding, etc.). Any client that can reach the app can delete arbitrary users and receive `204`.

Worth a separate look (pre-existing, outside this diff): `require_role` compares `ROLES.get(user)` where `user` is the *path* target, not an authenticated caller identity — so even before this change the decorator was not a real caller-authz check. Fixing cleanup-job access should introduce proper caller authentication and an explicit allowlist (e.g. admin **or** a dedicated service principal), not drop the gate.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
